claim_label: Competing priorities for government regulation of AI in schools
description: This conflict centers on the underlying values that should guide government regulation of AI in educational settings. The positions debate whether to prioritize rigorous safety testing, immediate pedagogical restrictions, or unrestricted access for workforce preparation.

instances.assertion: The government must require a one-year clinical trial to prove AI benefits outweigh harms before allowing it in schools.
Waiting for trials is a delay tactic; the government should immediately ban AI that gives answers and only allow AI that asks questions.
The government should not ban or delay AI, as doing so will leave students unprepared for the modern workforce.
Advocates for 'Transfer-of-Competency' audits and withdrawal-based performance testing to ensure cognitive independence.
Advocates for mandatory pre-deployment mechanistic interpretability audits to identify 'manipulative latent features' before harm occurs.
